paras.en: Outside of the DNA work, radiocarbon analysis of two threads collected from the Shroud's reliquary dated them to 1451–1622 CE and 1642–1800 CE, much later than the Shroud itself.
paras.zh: 在 DNA 工作之外，对从裹尸布圣物箱中收集的两条线进行放射性碳分析，将其追溯到公元 1451-1622 年和公元 1642-1800 年，比裹尸布本身晚得多。

paras.en: Those dates overlap with periods when the cloth is known to have been repaired: in 1534, after a fire at Chambéry, and again in 1694.
paras.zh: 这些日期与已知的布料修复时间重叠：1534 年，尚贝里火灾后，以及 1694 年。

paras.en: "Our findings constitute a novel and significant contribution to the field, thoroughly elucidating the biological traces left by centuries of social, cultural, and ecological engagement," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“我们的研究结果对该领域做出了新颖且重大的贡献，彻底阐明了几个世纪的社会、文化和生态参与留下的生物痕迹。”

paras.en: There are still a lot of questions remaining about the origin and authenticity of the Shroud of Turin, but this latest analysis adds plenty of background context – and shows that as scientific techniques improve, we can learn much more about this famous piece of cloth.
paras.zh: 关于都灵裹尸布的起源和真实性仍然存在很多问题，但最新的分析增加了大量的背景知识，并表明随着科学技术的进步，我们可以更多地了解这块著名的裹尸布。

paras.en: Further insights might be gathered by comparing the findings here with other ancient textiles and artifacts, according to the researchers, and these advanced methods have again proved how effective they are at identifying DNA signatures.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，通过将这里的发现与其他古代纺织品和文物进行比较，可以收集更多的见解，而这些先进的方法再次证明了它们在识别 DNA 特征方面的有效性。

paras.en: "The Shroud of Turin continues to fascinate historians, scientists, and the public," says Procopio.
paras.zh: “都灵裹尸布继续让历史学家、科学家和公众着迷，”普罗科皮奥说。

paras.en: "We're thrilled to reveal new information about the biological complexity preserved within samples collected almost 50 years ago by applying new cutting-edge forensic DNA technologies."
paras.zh: “我们很高兴能够通过应用新的尖端法医 DNA 技术揭示近 50 年前收集的样本中保存的生物复杂性的新信息。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Scientific Reports.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学报告》上。

articles.title: Blood Vessel Function Improves Within 1 Hour of Taking This Anti-Aging Supplement, Study Shows
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: One of the reasons that our health becomes more precarious as we age is that our blood vessels stiffen up and become less flexible, which can increase the risk of higher blood pressure and cardiovascular issues.
paras.zh: 随着年龄的增长，我们的健康变得更加不稳定的原因之一是我们的血管变硬且变得不那么灵活，这会增加患高血压和心血管问题的风险。

paras.en: Now researchers led by a team from the University of Surrey in the UK may have discovered a new way to counteract that gradual decline in blood vessel flexibility.
paras.zh: 现在，由英国萨里大学的一个团队领导的研究人员可能已经发现了一种抵消血管灵活性逐渐下降的新方法。

paras.en: They tested an already-available longevity and anti-aging supplement called Novos Core in 61 people aged over 40.
paras.zh: 他们在 61 名 40 岁以上的人身上测试了一种名为 Novos Core 的现有长寿和抗衰老补充剂。

paras.en: A little over half of the participants got Novos Core in a powdered formula, while the others were given a placebo powder.
paras.zh: 略多于一半的参与者服用了配方奶粉中的 Novos Core，而其他参与者则服用了安慰剂粉末。

paras.en: Both groups were followed for six months, while researchers kept tabs on the participants' cardiovascular health, including the work done by the lining of the blood vessels (the endothelium).
paras.zh: 两组患者都被跟踪了六个月，同时研究人员密切关注参与者的心血管健康状况，包括血管内皮（内皮）所做的工作。

paras.en: The final results showed a positive association between Novos Core and blood vessel function: not only did blood vessels start to behave in a more youthful way, some of the improvements were seen after just an hour.
paras.zh: 最终结果显示 Novos Core 与血管功能之间存在正相关关系：血管不仅开始表现得更年轻，而且仅仅一个小时后就看到了一些改善。

paras.en: "In apparently healthy adults, six months of daily intake of a multi-ingredient nutritional powder formulation was associated with favorable changes in vascular aging markers, including improved endothelial function, reduced device-derived arterial stiffness, and lower systolic blood pressure compared with control," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“在表面上健康的成年人中，每天摄入多成分营养粉配方的六个月与血管老化标志物的有利变化相关，包括改善内皮功能、减少设备源性动脉僵硬度以及与对照组相比降低收缩压。”

paras.en: For those in the Novos Core group, blood vessels got better at widening to allow more blood through, while arteries became softer and less stiff.
paras.zh: 对于 Novos Core 组的人来说，血管能够更好地扩张，以允许更多的血液通过，同时动脉变得更柔软、不那么僵硬。

paras.en: Blood pressure in these participants went down too – systolic blood pressure (the top number in readings) dropped by 6.1 mmHg more on average than for those in the placebo group.
paras.zh: 这些参与者的血压也下降了——收缩压（读数中最高的数字）比安慰剂组平均下降了 6.1 毫米汞柱。

paras.en: The 10-year estimated risk of heart attacks and strokes went down for the Novos Core group too, but it's important to bear in mind these events weren't tracked. There was no difference in low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol reduction between the two groups – the 'bad' cholesterol linked with poorer heart health.
paras.zh: Novos Core 组的 10 年心脏病发作和中风估计风险也有所下降，但重要的是要记住这些事件没有被跟踪。两组之间的低密度脂蛋白（LDL）胆固醇降低没有差异——“坏”胆固醇与较差的心脏健康有关。

paras.en: As an anti-aging supplement, Novos Core combines several ingredients that researchers have previously linked to slower biological aging, including magnesium, glucosamine, ginger extract, and vitamin C.
paras.zh: 作为一种抗衰老补充剂，Novos Core 结合了研究人​​员之前认为可以减缓生物衰老的多种成分，包括镁、葡萄糖胺、生姜提取物和维生素 C。

paras.en: "The formulation evaluated in the present study was selected to combine ingredients with prior evidence of relevance to complementary biological domains implicated in aging and vascular dysfunction, including endothelial function, redox balance, inflammatory signaling, metabolic regulation, and vascular tone," write the researchers.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“本研究中评估的配方被选择将成分与先前证据相结合，这些证据与衰老和血管功能障碍相关的互补生物领域相关，包括内皮功能、氧化还原平衡、炎症信号、代谢调节和血管张力。”

paras.en: Now we know that some of those ingredients are apparently acting on blood vessel function, which may explain why they're already associated with the body's aging process and better cardiovascular health.
paras.zh: 现在我们知道其中一些成分显然对血管功能起作用，这可以解释为什么它们已经与身体的衰老过程和更好的心血管健康相关。

paras.en: There's still plenty of research work left to be done, though. The blood health markers that the study looked at are significant, but the participants weren't followed to see who did or didn't go on to have heart health problems in the future.
paras.zh: 不过，仍有大量研究工作有待完成。该研究考察的血液健康指标很重要，但没有对参与者进行跟踪，看看谁在未来会出现或不会出现心脏健康问题。

paras.en: "The findings provide an interesting proof of concept, but the important next step is to understand the underlying biology and establish whether changes in cardiovascular biomarkers translate into meaningful longer-term health benefits," says Juliet Wright, the Founding Dean of Medicine at the University of Surrey, who wasn't directly involved in the research.
paras.zh: “这些发现提供了一个有趣的概念证明，但重要的下一步是了解潜在的生物学，并确定心血管生物标志物的变化是否转化为有意义的长期健康益处，”萨里大学医学院创始院长朱丽叶·赖特（Juliet Wright）说，她没有直接参与这项研究。

paras.en: Further research would be able to look at larger, more diverse groups of people, and perhaps tease out the effects of the different ingredients in Novos Core. Right now, it's tricky to know which of its various compounds are having the most effect.
paras.zh: 进一步的研究将能够观察更大、更多样化的人群，或许还能弄清楚 Novos Core 中不同成分的影响。目前，很难知道其中哪种化合物最有效。

paras.en: It's also worth noting that the funding for the research came from the Novos company that makes Novos Core, though the paper declares that Novos "had no role" in the study design, or the "collection, primary analysis or interpretation of data".
paras.zh: 还值得注意的是，该研究的资金来自生产 Novos Core 的 Novos 公司，尽管该论文声称 Novos 在研究设计或“数据的收集、初步分析或解释”中“没有任何作用”。

paras.en: Related: A Cheap Daily Supplement Seems to Boost Brain Function in Older Adults
paras.zh: 相关：廉价的每日补充剂似乎可以增强老年人的大脑功能

paras.en: "These findings are encouraging," says Christian Heiss, a professor of cardiovascular medicine at the University of Surrey.
paras.zh: “这些发现令人鼓舞，”萨里大学心血管医学教授克里斯蒂安·海斯说。

paras.en: "We now need larger studies to understand the mechanisms involved and, importantly, whether these changes translate into longer-term health benefits."
paras.zh: “我们现在需要更大规模的研究来了解所涉及的机制，更重要的是，了解这些变化是否会转化为长期的健康益处。”

paras.en: The research has been published in European Heart Journal Open.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《欧洲心脏杂志开放》上。

articles.title: A Cheap Daily Supplement Seems to Boost Brain Function in Older Adults
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Cheap daily supplements are changing how scientists view the gut and its connection to the brain.
paras.zh: 廉价的日常补充剂正在改变科学家对肠道及其与大脑的联系的看法。

paras.en: In 2024, a rigorous twin study published in Nature Communications found that taking daily protein and prebiotic supplements can improve memory test scores in people over age 60.
paras.zh: 2024 年，《自然通讯》发表的一项严格的双胞胎研究发现，每日服用蛋白质和益生元补充剂可以提高 60 岁以上人群的记忆力测试成绩。

paras.en: The study has been cited more than 100 times since, and the idea has inspired whole new clinical trials investigating how some supplements may protect against dementia.
paras.zh: 自那以后，这项研究已被引用超过 100 次，这个想法激发了全新的临床试验，研究某些补充剂如何预防痴呆症。

paras.en: Later that year, scientists at Wageningen University in the Netherlands launched the PRECODE clinical trial, which stands for Gut-brain Health Effects of PREbiotics in Older Adults With Suspected COgnitive DEcline.
paras.zh: 同年晚些时候，荷兰瓦赫宁根大学的科学家启动了 PRECODE 临床试验，该试验代表益生元对疑似认知能力下降的老年人的肠脑健康影响。

paras.en: It's the first human study to investigate the combined cognitive and microbial effects of three distinct dietary fibers: chicory inulin, resistant dextrin, and seaweed polysaccharide, compared to a placebo (maltodextrin).
paras.zh: 这是第一项人体研究，调查三种不同膳食纤维（菊苣菊粉、抗性糊精和海藻多糖）与安慰剂（麦芽糖糊精）相比对认知和微生物的综合影响。

paras.en: For 26 weeks, participants over 60 have consumed these dietary fibers twice a day, mixed into water, tea, or coffee, and they have had regular brain scans and cognitive tests to track how they are faring.
paras.zh: 在 26 周的时间里，60 岁以上的参与者每天两次食用这些膳食纤维，将其混合到水、茶或咖啡中，并且他们定期进行脑部扫描和认知测试，以跟踪他们的情况。

paras.en: We'll know more in 2027 when the trial finishes.
paras.zh: 2027 年审判结束后我们将会了解更多信息。

paras.en: Inulin, a dietary fiber in the fructan class, is the same dietary supplement that proved so good for the brain in that first 2024 twin study.
paras.zh: 菊粉是一种果聚糖类膳食纤维，在 2024 年的第一项双胞胎研究中证明它对大脑非常有益。

paras.en: Watch the video below for a summary of the 2024 study:
paras.zh: 观看下面的视频，了解 2024 年研究的摘要：

paras.en: During that double-blind trial, researchers tested two inexpensive plant-fiber prebiotics that are available over the counter in many countries.
paras.zh: 在那次双盲试验中，研究人员测试了两种廉价的植物纤维益生元，这些益生元在许多国家都可以在柜台购买。

paras.en: The other, fructooligosaccharide (FOS), is a plant carbohydrate often used as a natural low-calorie sweetener.
paras.zh: 另一种是低聚果糖（FOS），是一种植物碳水化合物，通常用作天然低热量甜味剂。

paras.en: To look into how these supplements affected the aging brain, researchers at King's College London enrolled 36 pairs of twins, all at least 60 years old.
paras.zh: 为了研究这些补充剂如何影响衰老的大脑，伦敦国王学院的研究人员招募了 36 对双胞胎，他们的年龄都至少 60 岁。

paras.en: Each duo was randomly split: one twin received a daily prebiotic mixed into protein powder, while the other received a placebo powder.
paras.zh: 每对双胞胎被随机分成：双胞胎中的一个每天服用混合在蛋白粉中的益生元，而另一个则服用安慰剂粉。

paras.en: The twins who unknowingly took inulin or FOS generally scored higher on a cognitive test three months later.
paras.zh: 在不知情的情况下服用菊粉或低聚果糖的双胞胎在三个月后的认知测试中通常得分更高。

paras.en: What's more, the daily fiber supplements were linked to subtle changes in the gut microbiome between twins.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，每日纤维补充剂与双胞胎肠道微生物群的微妙变化有关。

paras.en: The beneficial Bifidobacterium, for instance, was more plentiful in those taking inulin or FOS.
paras.zh: 例如，服用菊粉或低聚果糖的人体内有益的​​双歧杆菌含量更高。

paras.en: Studies on mice suggest that Bifidobacterium reduces cognitive deficits by regulating gut-brain connections.
paras.zh: 对小鼠的研究表明，双歧杆菌通过调节肠脑连接来减少认知缺陷。

paras.en: "We are excited to see these changes in just 12 weeks. This holds huge promise for enhancing brain health and memory in our aging population," said Mary Ni Lochlainn, a geriatric medicine researcher at King's College London, when the findings were published in 2024.
paras.zh: “我们很高兴在短短 12 周内看到这些变化。这对于增强老年人的大脑健康和记忆力有着巨大的希望，”伦敦国王学院老年医学研究员 Mary Ni Lochlainn 在 2024 年发表研究结果时说道。

paras.en: "Unlocking the secrets of the gut-brain axis could offer new approaches for living more healthily for longer."
paras.zh: “解开肠脑轴的秘密可以为更健康、更长久地生活提供新方法。”

paras.en: King's College London (KCL) is home to the UK's largest adult twin registry, and twin studies are highly valuable when it comes to differentiating between the effects of genetics and the environment on human health.
paras.zh: 伦敦国王学院 (KCL) 是英国最大的成人双胞胎登记处，双胞胎研究对于区分遗传和环境对人类健康的影响非常有价值。

paras.en: Past studies on rodents suggest that high-fiber supplements, such as inulin and FOS, can 'feed' the colon's microbiome, allowing 'good' bacteria to thrive.
paras.zh: 过去对啮齿动物的研究表明，高纤维补充剂，如菊粉和低聚果糖，可以“喂养”结肠的微生物群，让“好”细菌茁壮成长。

paras.en: Some of these bacterial players are also linked to improved cognitive function in both mice and humans.
paras.zh: 其中一些细菌也与小鼠和人类认知功能的改善有关。

paras.en: Some experts are now so convinced by the results that they refer to the gut as the body's 'second brain'.
paras.zh: 现在，一些专家对这些结果深信不疑，他们将肠道称为人体的“第二大脑”。

paras.en: But the way these two nervous systems work together remains a mystery.
paras.zh: 但这两个神经系统如何协同工作仍然是个谜。

paras.en: The twin study at KCL hints that consuming certain 'brain foods' could be a promising way to treat cognitive decline, adding to research suggesting key nutrients may be able to slow its progress.
paras.zh: 伦敦皇家学院的双胞胎研究暗示，食用某些“健脑食品”可能是治疗认知能力下降的一种有前途的方法，并补充了表明关键营养素可能能够减缓其进展的研究。

paras.en: "These plant fibers, which are cheap and available over the counter, could benefit a wide group of people in these cash-strapped times. They are safe and acceptable too," said geriatrician Claire Steves at KCL.
paras.zh: “这些植物纤维价格便宜，可以在柜台上买到，在这个现金短缺的时代可以让很多人受益。它们也安全且可以接受，”伦敦国王学院的老年病学家克莱尔·史蒂夫斯说。

paras.en: "Our next task is to see whether these effects are sustained over longer periods and in larger groups of people."
paras.zh: “我们的下一个任务是看看这些影响是否会在更长的时间内、在更大的人群中持续存在。”

paras.en: That's what the PRECODE trial seeks to address.
paras.zh: 这就是 PRECODE 试验试图解决的问题。

paras.en: The trial investigators hope this ongoing study into fiber supplements will "provide an in-depth evaluation of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in older adults, at risk of cognitive decline."
paras.zh: 试验研究人员希望这项正在进行的纤维补充剂研究能够“对面临认知能力下降风险的老年人的微生物群-肠-脑轴进行深入评估”。

paras.en: Related: One Common Vitamin May Lower Toxic Alzheimer's Proteins, Research Suggests
paras.zh: 相关：研究表明，一种常见的维生素可以降低有毒的阿尔茨海默氏症蛋白质

paras.en: In 2025, researchers reported that in humans and mice, a lower Bifidobacterium-to-Akkermansia ratio in the gut microbiome is linked to multiple sclerosis, and this imbalance was also associated with more severe disease.
paras.zh: 2025 年，研究人员报告称，在人类和小鼠中，肠道微生物组中双歧杆菌与阿克曼氏菌的比率较低与多发性硬化症有关，而这种不平衡也与更严重的疾病有关。

paras.en: Whether these deficiencies can be remedied with supplements, however, remains unknown.
paras.zh: 然而，这些缺陷是否可以通过补充剂来弥补仍然未知。

paras.en: The gut has its fingers in many bodily 'pies', including the immune system and the central nervous system.
paras.zh: 肠道参与了许多身体“馅饼”，包括免疫系统和中枢神经系统。

paras.en: Feeding its microbiome certain prebiotics and probiotics could open the door to treating a plethora of illnesses and diseases.
paras.zh: 向其微生物组喂食某些益生元和益生菌可以为治疗多种疾病打开大门。

paras.en: The PRECODE trial could give us a first taste of that possibility.
paras.zh: PRECODE 试验可以让我们第一次尝到这种可能性。

paras.en: The twin study was published in Nature Communications.
paras.zh: 这项双胞胎研究发表在《自然通讯》上。

articles.title: Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation

paras.en: Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation
paras.zh: 两个来自创世之初的怪物黑洞无法解释

paras.en: Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy (AURA)
paras.zh: 天文学研究大学协会 (AURA)

paras.en: Astronomers have discovered the oldest known compact pair of quasars, powered by two enormous black holes that existed just 900 million years after the Big Bang. Weighing an astonishing 1.5 billion and 400 million times the mass of the Sun, these cosmic giants somehow grew to incredible sizes far earlier than current theories can explain.
paras.zh: 天文学家发现了已知最古老的致密类星体对，它们由大爆炸后仅 9 亿年就存在的两个巨大黑洞提供动力。这些宇宙巨星的质量惊人，分别是太阳质量的 15 亿倍和 4 亿倍，它们以某种方式增长到令人难以置信的尺寸，远远早于当前理论所能解释的时间。

paras.en: Astronomers have identified an extraordinary pair of quasars dating back to just 900 million years after the Big Bang. Each is powered by an enormous black hole that somehow grew to an astonishing size when the Universe was still in its infancy. Scientists have no definitive explanation for how these two cosmic giants became so massive so quickly. The remarkable pair has been given the Hawaiian name Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.
paras.zh: 天文学家发现了一对非凡的类星体，其历史可以追溯到大爆炸后仅 9 亿年。每一个都由一个巨大的黑洞提供动力，当宇宙还处于婴儿期时，这个黑洞不知何故就增长到了惊人的大小。对于这两个宇宙巨星为何如此迅速地变得如此巨大，科学家们还没有明确的解释。这对非凡的情侣被赋予了夏威夷语名字 Nāpōwawa'enakaulua。

paras.en: An international research team has discovered the most distant compact pair of quasars ever observed, offering a rare glimpse into the earliest stages of cosmic history. Officially designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the pair also holds the record for the closest separation between two known quasars from the early period known as cosmic dawn.
paras.zh: 一个国际研究小组发现了迄今为止观测到的最遥远的致密类星体对，为了解宇宙历史的最早阶段提供了难得的机会。官方命名为 J1602+4228AB，绰号为 Nāpōwawā´enakaulua，这对星体还保持着早期宇宙黎明时期两个已知类星体之间最接近距离的记录。

paras.en: Although astronomers believe paired quasars should be relatively common, finding and studying them is exceptionally difficult. Discovering two so close together, especially from such an early period in the Universe's history, makes this finding particularly remarkable.
paras.zh: 尽管天文学家认为成对类星体应该相对常见，但发现和研究它们却异常困难。发现两个距离如此之近，尤其是在宇宙历史的如此早期阶段，使这一发现显得尤为引人注目。

paras.en: The discovery was made possible by combining observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Gemini North telescope on Maunakea, a dormant volcano in Hawai'i. The research was led by Silvia Onorato, a postdoctoral research associate at NSF NOIRLab, and is described in a paper published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.
paras.zh: 这一发现是通过詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜（JWST）和夏威夷莫纳克亚休眠火山上的双子座北望远镜的观测相结合而实现的。这项研究由 NSF NOIRLab 博士后研究员 Silvia Onorato 领导，并在《天体物理学杂志快报》上发表的一篇论文中进行了描述。

paras.en: Gemini North is one of the two telescopes that make up the International Gemini Observatory. Operated by NSF NOIRLab, the observatory is an international partnership led by the U.S. National Science Foundation, with participation from Canada, Chile, Brazil, Argentina, and the Republic of Korea.
paras.zh: 双子座北站是组成国际双子座天文台的两座望远镜之一。该天文台由 NSF NOIRLab 运营，是一个由美国国家科学基金会领导、加拿大、智利、巴西、阿根廷和韩国参与的国际合作项目。

paras.en: How Giant Black Holes Formed in the Early Universe
paras.zh: 早期宇宙中巨大的黑洞是如何形成的

paras.en: During the first billion years after the Big Bang, the Universe underwent a period of extraordinary transformation. Vast concentrations of invisible matter, known as dark matter halos, collapsed under gravity. The earliest galaxies began producing stars, while increasingly massive galaxies developed the first supermassive black holes at their centers.
paras.zh: 在大爆炸后的最初十亿年里，宇宙经历了一段非凡的转变时期。大量不可见物质（称为暗物质晕）在重力作用下崩溃。最早的星系开始产生恒星，而质量越来越大的星系在其中心形成了第一个超大质量黑洞。

paras.en: As galaxies passed near one another, collided, and sometimes merged, enormous quantities of gas and stars became available to feed their central black holes. Some of the material falling toward these black holes released tremendous amounts of energy. This process, known as accretion, could generate radiation so intense that the glowing region surrounding a black hole outshone every star in its host galaxy.
paras.zh: 当星系彼此靠近、碰撞，有时甚至合并时，大量的气体和恒星就可以为它们的中心黑洞提供营养。一些落向黑洞的物质释放出巨大的能量。这个过程被称为吸积，可以产生如此强烈的辐射，以至于黑洞周围的发光区域比其宿主星系中的每一颗恒星都更亮。

paras.en: Astronomers call these extraordinarily luminous objects quasars.
paras.zh: 天文学家将这些异常发光的物体称为类星体。

paras.en: Because galaxy encounters and mergers occur frequently throughout the Universe, researchers expect many quasars to exist in pairs separated by distances smaller than the typical diameter of a galaxy. Yet detecting these systems has remained a major challenge.
paras.zh: 由于星系相遇和合并在整个宇宙中频繁发生，研究人员预计许多类星体成对存在，其间隔距离小于星系的典型直径。然而检测这些系统仍然是一个重大挑战。

paras.en: One reason is that a supermassive black hole spends only a relatively brief period in its bright "quasar phase." Another is the enormous distance separating ancient quasars from Earth, which makes them appear extremely faint to ground-based telescopes. Even when both objects are visible, their close proximity can make it difficult to distinguish one from the other.
paras.zh: 原因之一是超大质量黑洞在其明亮的“类星体阶段”仅花费相对较短的时间。另一个原因是古代类星体与地球之间的距离巨大，这使得它们对于地面望远镜来说显得极其微弱。即使两个物体都可见，但它们的距离太近也会导致很难区分另一个物体。

paras.en: Two Monster Black Holes That Grew Too Big, Too Fast
paras.zh: 两个增长太大、太快的怪物黑洞

paras.en: Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua stands out because it is only the third known quasar pair from cosmic dawn. More importantly, its two black holes were already so enormous at such an early stage of cosmic history that existing theories cannot definitively explain their growth.
paras.zh: Nāpōwawa'enakaulua 之所以引人注目，是因为它是宇宙黎明以来已知的第三对类星体。更重要的是，它的两个黑洞在宇宙历史的早期阶段就已经非常巨大，现有的理论无法明确解释它们的增长。

paras.en: The black holes are separated by approximately 18,100 light-years, equivalent to about one-fifth the diameter of the Milky Way. One has an estimated mass of 1.5 billion Suns, while the other weighs approximately 400 million solar masses.
paras.zh: 黑洞相距约 18,100 光年，相当于银河系直径的五分之一左右。据估计，其中一颗的质量为 15 亿个太阳质量，而另一个的重量约为 4 亿个太阳质量。

paras.en: Astronomers see the pair as it appeared only 900 million years after the Big Bang, when the Universe was still populated by relatively young stars, galaxies, and black holes. Finding two black holes comparable in mass to many present-day supermassive black holes at this early time raises difficult questions about how quickly the first enormous cosmic structures could assemble.
paras.zh: 天文学家看到的这对星系是在大爆炸后仅 9 亿年出现的，当时宇宙中仍然充满了相对年轻的恒星、星系和黑洞。在这么早的时间发现两个质量与当今许多超大质量黑洞相当的黑洞，提出了关于第一个巨大的宇宙结构能够以多快的速度聚集的难题。

paras.en: "There is no definitive theoretical explanation for how a single one of these giant quasars exists so early in the age of our Universe, much less two," says Onorato. "We observed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua at a time when the Universe was only a thirteenth of its age and astonishingly, its supermassive black holes are just as massive as those we see today."
paras.zh: 奥诺拉托说：“对于这些巨大类星体中的单个类星体如何在我们的宇宙时代如此早期存在，目前还没有明确的理论解释，更不用说两个了。” “我们观测纳波瓦瓦埃纳卡乌鲁亚时，宇宙的年龄仅为其年龄的十三分之一，令人惊讶的是，它的超大质量黑洞与我们今天看到的黑洞一样大。”

paras.en: The pair's Hawaiian name reflects the extraordinary forces involved. Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua translates to "Two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the Universe."
paras.zh: 这对夫妇的夏威夷名字反映了所涉及的非凡力量。 Nāpōwawā´enakaulua 的意思是“两个深不可测的强大黑暗天体，在热量的光辉中将能量轮回宇宙”。

paras.en: The name was developed through the A Hua He Inoa program, a collaboration involving the ʻImiloa Astronomy Center of Hawaiʻi and the University of Hawai'i's Ka Haka ʻUla O Keʻelikōlani (Hawaiian Language College).[1]
paras.zh: 该名称是通过 A Hua He Inoa 计划开发的，该计划是夏威夷伊米洛亚天文中心和夏威夷大学 Ka Haka ´Ula O Ke´elikōlani（夏威夷语言学院）的合作项目。[1]

paras.en: How James Webb and Gemini North Revealed the Hidden Pair
paras.zh: 詹姆斯·韦伯和双子座诺斯如何揭示隐藏的一对

paras.en: The discovery began with data collected by the Aether survey, a JWST research program designed to identify and characterize objects from the early Universe. The project is led by Emanuele Paolo Farina, an Associate Scientist at NSF NOIRLab/Gemini.
paras.zh: 这一发现始于“以太调查”收集的数据，“以太调查”是 JWST 的一项研究计划，旨在识别和表征早期宇宙中的物体。该项目由 NSF NOIRLab/Gemini 的副科学家 Emanuele Paolo Farina 领导。

paras.en: Using JWST's Near-Infrared Spectrograph Integral Field Unit, the survey assembled observations of 200 quasars. That sample represents approximately 43% of all quasars known from this period of cosmic history.
paras.zh: 该调查利用 JWST 的近红外光谱仪整体现场装置收集了 200 个类星体的观测结果。该样本约占这段宇宙历史时期已知的所有类星体的 43%。

paras.en: While visually examining the survey data, researchers noticed something unexpected. A previously identified quasar, J1602+4228A, appeared to have a companion.
paras.zh: 在目视检查调查数据时，研究人员发现了一些意想不到的事情。之前发现的一颗类星体 J1602+4228A 似乎有一个伴星。

paras.en: To investigate, the team turned to Gemini North's Gemini Near-Infrared Spectrograph (GNIRS). These observations allowed astronomers to distinguish the two quasars individually, providing crucial evidence about the nature of the system.
paras.zh: 为了进行调查，研究小组求助于 Gemini North 的 Gemini 近红外光谱仪 (GNIRS)。这些观测结果使天文学家能够单独区分两个类星体，为该系统的性质提供了重要证据。

paras.en: Obtaining those measurements was an exceptional achievement. The objects are separated by such a small apparent distance, and the companion J1602+4228B is so faint, that resolving them with a telescope on Earth was expected to be nearly impossible.
paras.zh: 获得这些测量结果是一项非凡的成就。这些物体之间的视距如此之小，而且伴星 J1602+4228B 又如此微弱，以至于用地球上的望远镜来分辨它们几乎是不可能的。

paras.en: Fortunately, the researchers benefited from exceptionally favorable observing conditions on Maunakea. Clear skies and unusually sharp atmospheric conditions enabled them to gather the necessary observations in just two nights.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，研究人员受益于莫纳克亚山异常有利的观测条件。晴朗的天空和异常尖锐的大气条件使他们能够在短短两个晚上收集必要的观测结果。

paras.en: "The sky over Maunakea was so clean and sharp that we managed to collect the data in only two nights," says Onorato.
paras.zh: 奥诺拉托说：“莫纳克亚上空的天空是如此干净和清晰，我们只用了两个晚上就收集到了数据。”

paras.en: The team also used Gemini North's Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph (GMOS) to gather additional information about the system and refine their understanding of the two quasars.[2]
paras.zh: 该团队还使用 Gemini North 的 Gemini 多目标摄谱仪 (GMOS) 收集有关该系统的更多信息，并完善他们对两个类星体的理解。 [2]

paras.en: A New Clue to the Universe's First Giant Galaxies
paras.zh: 宇宙第一个巨型星系的新线索

paras.en: Exactly how Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua formed remains unknown. However, the researchers believe its extraordinary properties could point to an unusually dense concentration of matter in the early Universe.
paras.zh: Nāpōwawa'enakaulua 究竟是如何形成的仍然未知。然而，研究人员认为，其非凡的特性可能表明早期宇宙中物质浓度异常密集。

paras.en: In such an environment, frequent interactions between young galaxies may have provided enormous supplies of gas, simultaneously accelerating the birth of stars and fueling rapid growth of the black holes at their centers.
paras.zh: 在这样的环境中，年轻星系之间的频繁相互作用可能提供了大量的气体供应，同时加速了恒星的诞生，并促进了其中心黑洞的快速增长。

paras.en: If this interpretation is correct, the quasar pair could help scientists understand how the earliest massive galaxies developed alongside their central supermassive black holes.
paras.zh: 如果这种解释是正确的，这对类星体可以帮助科学家了解最早的大质量星系是如何与它们的中心超大质量黑洞一起发展的。

paras.en: "Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua is a really unique environment," says Onorato. "It's a laboratory for astronomers to study how the very first massive galaxies and their central black holes assembled together through direct galaxy interactions during these early times."
paras.zh: “Nāpōwawā´enakaulua 是一个非常独特的环境，”奥诺拉托说。 “这是一个天文学家的实验室，用于研究早期大质量星系及其中心黑洞如何通过直接星系相互作用聚集在一起。”

paras.en: - The A Hua He Inoa (AHHI) program draws on traditional Hawaiian naming practices and frequently involves students, educators, and community members fluent in 'Ōlelo Hawaiʻi, the Indigenous language of Hawaiʻi. The name Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua was created by Larry Kimura, a professor at Ka Haka ʻUla O Keʻelikōlani. Its components describe the physical characteristics of the quasar pair: Nā (plural indicator), Pō (fathomless powerful darkness) symbolizes the supermassive black holes, Wawā (reincarnation or procreation as referenced from hānau wawā in Pukui-Elbert (1986) dictionary), ʻEna (brilliance of heat) describes the intense radiation released by matter falling toward the black holes, and Kaulua (double or pair) identifies the system as two quasars. The name also connects to two earlier astronomical objects named through A Hua He Inoa. These are Pōwehi, associated with the first image of a black hole in 2019, and Pōniuāʻena, which was the most distant known quasar when it was discovered in 2020.
paras.zh: - A Hua He Inoa (AHHI) 计划借鉴了传统的夏威夷命名做法，经常涉及精通夏威夷原住语言“Ōlelo Hawai´i”的学生、教育工作者和社区成员。 Nāpōwawa'enakaulua 这个名字是由 Ka Haka 'Ula O Ke'elikōlani 教授拉里·木村 (Larry Kimura) 创建的。它的组成部分描述了类星体对的物理特征：Nā（复数指示符）、Pō（深不可测的强大黑暗）象征着超大质量黑洞、Wawā（转世或繁殖，参考 Pukui-Elbert (1986) 词典中的 hānau wawā）、'Ena（热光）描述了落向黑洞的物质释放的强烈辐射，Kaulua（双或对）将系统标识为两个类星体类星体。这个名字还与两个早期的天体有关，这些天体是通过阿华赫伊诺阿（A Hua He Inoa）命名的。它们是与 2019 年首张黑洞图像相关的 Pōwehi，以及 2020 年发现时已知最遥远的类星体 Pōniuā´ena。

paras.en: - Researchers used GMOS observations to examine an alternative possibility involving gravitational lensing. This occurs when the gravity of an intervening object bends and magnifies light from a more distant source, potentially creating multiple images of the same object. The team investigated whether such an effect might explain the appearance of the second, fainter quasar. Differences between the spectra of the two objects favor the interpretation that they are separate physical quasars. However, additional gravitational lens modeling will be required before the lensing possibility can be definitively excluded.
paras.zh: - 研究人员使用 GMOS 观测来检验涉及引力透镜的另一种可能性。当介入物体的重力弯曲并放大来自较远光源的光时，就会发生这种情况，可能会产生同一物体的多个图像。研究小组研究了这种效应是否可以解释第二个较暗的类星体的出现。两个物体光谱之间的差异有利于将它们解释为独立的物理类星体。然而，在明确排除透镜效应之前，还需要额外的引力透镜模型。

paras.en: Materials provided by Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy (AURA). Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由天文学研究大学协会 (AURA) 提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

articles.title: A galactic shock wave could rewrite the map of the Milky Way

paras.en: A galactic shock wave could rewrite the map of the Milky Way
paras.zh: 银河冲击波可能改写银河系地图

paras.en: A surprising discovery suggests the Milky Way may be making stars in places where most galaxies cannot. Scientists found evidence that a massive rotating structure near the galactic center is creating powerful shock waves that trigger star formation rather than suppress it. Even more unexpectedly, part of the Norma spiral arm may not be a spiral arm at all, but a vast region where new stars are being born.
paras.zh: 一项令人惊讶的发现表明，银河系可能正在大多数星系无法形成恒星的地方形成恒星。科学家发现证据表明，银河系中心附近的一个巨大旋转结构正在产生强大的冲击波，从而引发而不是抑制恒星的形成。更令人意想不到的是，诺玛旋臂的一部分可能根本就不是旋臂，而是一片正在诞生新恒星的广阔区域。

paras.en: New research suggests the Milky Way produces stars in an unexpected location, revealing a surprising difference between our galaxy and most of its neighbors. The findings also raise questions about a familiar feature of the Milky Way, suggesting that part of what astronomers have long considered a spiral arm may actually be something else.
paras.zh: 新的研究表明，银河系在一个意想不到的位置产生了恒星，揭示了我们的星系和它的大多数邻居之间的惊人差异。这些发现还对银河系的一个常见特征提出了疑问，表明天文学家长期以来认为的旋臂的一部分实际上可能是其他东西。

paras.en: The discovery comes from research led by a University of Sydney PhD student, who found evidence that a massive rotating structure of stars near the galactic center is generating powerful shock waves through surrounding clouds of gas. These waves squeeze the gas together, creating conditions that allow new stars to form in a region where such intense forces usually prevent their birth.
paras.zh: 这一发现来自悉尼大学一名博士生领导的研究，他发现证据表明，银河系中心附近的巨大旋转恒星结构正在通过周围的气体云产生强大的冲击波。这些波将气体挤压在一起，为新恒星在通常会阻止其诞生的区域形成创造了条件。

paras.en: Published in Nature Astronomy, the study also casts doubt on the nature of the Norma spiral arm, a feature of the Milky Way named for the constellation Norma as seen from Earth.
paras.zh: 这项发表在《自然天文学》上的研究还对诺玛旋臂的性质提出了质疑，诺玛旋臂是银河系的一个特征，以从地球上看到的诺玛星座命名。

paras.en: Lead author Dr. Hillary Davis, who recently completed her PhD at the University of Sydney's School of Physics and Sydney Institute for Astronomy, said the research provides new insights into the structures near the galactic center and how gas moves around them.
paras.zh: 主要作者希拉里·戴维斯博士最近在悉尼大学物理学院和悉尼天文研究所完成了博士学位，她表示，这项研究为了解银河系中心附近的结构以及气体在其周围的运动方式提供了新的见解。

paras.en: "At its heart, star formation is a process we understand from everyday physics. Forces set matter in motion. In this case gas is compressed, and that compression can create the conditions for new stars to be born on a massive scale," Dr. Davis said.
paras.zh: 戴维斯博士说：“从本质上讲，恒星形成是我们从日常物理学中理解的一个过程。力使物质运动。在这种情况下，气体被压缩，而这种压缩可以为新恒星的大规模诞生创造条件。”

paras.en: "In most similar galaxies, star formation very commonly occurs along spiral arms. What's extraordinary is seeing this happen in a different region of our Galaxy, where shocks are usually so strong that star formation is often suppressed."
paras.zh: “在大多数类似的星系中，恒星形成通常沿着旋臂发生。令人惊奇的是，这种情况发生在我们银河系的另一个区域，那里的冲击通常非常强烈，以至于恒星的形成经常受到抑制。”

paras.en: A Hidden Star Factory at the Heart of the Milky Way
paras.zh: 银河系中心隐藏的恒星工厂

paras.en: The Milky Way belongs to a class of galaxies known as barred spiral galaxies. Unlike galaxies with only a central concentration of stars and surrounding spiral arms, these systems contain an elongated structure of stars stretching across their central region. In our galaxy, this structure is called the Galactic bar.
paras.zh: 银河系属于一类被称为棒旋星系的星系。与只有中心集中的恒星和周围旋臂的星系不同，这些系统包含横跨其中心区域的细长恒星结构。在我们的银河系中，这种结构被称为银河棒。

paras.en: As the bar rotates, its gravity influences nearby gas, driving it into powerful shock fronts. These fronts compress the gas in much the same way that a shock wave compresses air.
paras.zh: 当棒旋转时，它的重力会影响附近的气体，将其推入强大的激波前沿。这些前沿压缩气体的方式与冲击波压缩空气的方式非常相似。

paras.en: Studying this structure from Earth is particularly difficult because we are located inside the Milky Way rather than viewing it from the outside. Large amounts of cosmic dust also block our view of the galactic center.
paras.zh: 从地球上研究这种结构特别困难，因为我们位于银河系内部，而不是从外部观察它。大量的宇宙尘埃也阻挡了我们观察银河系中心的视线。

paras.en: "The Galactic bar cannot be easily observed because of a combination of our position in the Galaxy and dust obscuring our view," Dr. Davis said.
paras.zh: 戴维斯博士说：“由于我们在银河系中的位置和灰尘遮蔽了我们的视野，银河棒不容易被观察到。”

paras.en: "As a result, the bar's properties have been highly debated."
paras.zh: “因此，酒吧的属性引起了激烈的争论。”

paras.en: Observations of other barred galaxies have shown that these shock fronts generally inhibit the formation of new stars, even in regions containing abundant gas. The intense conditions make it difficult for the gas to collapse into stars.
paras.zh: 对其他棒星系的观测表明，这些激波锋面通常会抑制新恒星的形成，即使在含有丰富气体的区域也是如此。恶劣的条件使得气体很难塌缩成恒星。

paras.en: However, the new findings indicate that the Milky Way may behave differently. Although it is not the only known example, our galaxy appears to belong to a relatively small group in which substantial star formation takes place along the shock fronts of the central bar.
paras.zh: 然而，新的发现表明银河系的行为可能有所不同。尽管这不是唯一已知的例子，但我们的星系似乎属于一个相对较小的星系团，其中大量的恒星形成是沿着中央棒的激波前沿发生的。

paras.en: "We believe that the Milky Way's bar has star formation occurring along its shock front, which is uncommon for most bars in nearby galaxies," Dr. Davis said.
paras.zh: 戴维斯博士说：“我们认为，银河系的棒状体沿着其激波前沿发生了恒星形成，这对于附近星系的大多数棒状体来说并不常见。”

paras.en: A Milky Way Spiral Arm May Not Be What It Seems
paras.zh: 银河系的旋臂可能并非看起来那样

paras.en: To investigate this unusual activity, the research team compared detailed computer simulations showing how galaxies change over billions of years with astronomical observations of regions where massive stars are forming.
paras.zh: 为了调查这种不寻常的活动，研究小组将详细的计算机模拟（显示星系在数十亿年间如何变化）与对大质量恒星形成区域的天文观测进行了比较。

paras.en: A crucial part of the evidence came from masers, naturally occurring sources that emit highly concentrated microwave radiation. These emissions are associated with the formation of massive stars and operate on a principle similar to lasers, but at microwave wavelengths.
paras.zh: 证据的一个关键部分来自微波激射器，这是一种发射高度集中微波辐射的天然来源。这些发射与大质量恒星的形成有关，其工作原理类似于激光，但波长为微波。

paras.en: By examining the positions of these masers, the researchers uncovered a striking match between actual observations and the locations of shock fronts predicted by their simulations.
paras.zh: 通过检查这些微波激射器的位置，研究人员发现实际观测结果与模拟预测的激波锋位置之间存在惊人的匹配。

paras.en: "We found that masers previously associated with the Norma arm closely align with the shock front predicted by our simulations," Dr. Davis said. "This suggests that at least part of the so-called Norma arm may not be a spiral arm at all, but a region of star formation along the leading edge of the Galactic bar.
paras.zh: 戴维斯博士说：“我们发现，先前与诺玛臂相关的脉泽与我们模拟预测的激波锋面密切相关。” “这表明，所谓的诺玛臂的至少一部分可能根本不是旋臂，而是沿着银条前缘的恒星形成区域。

paras.en: "This raises questions about the Galaxy's spiral structure, and the bar region of the Milky Way, which needs further investigation," she said.
paras.zh: “这引发了关于银河系螺旋结构和银河系条形区域的问题，需要进一步调查，”她说。

paras.en: The possibility is significant because it suggests that some of the star formation previously attributed to the Norma spiral arm could instead be occurring along the central bar. If confirmed, this interpretation would change how astronomers understand the arrangement of stars and gas in that part of the Milky Way.
paras.zh: 这种可能性很重要，因为它表明之前归因于诺玛旋臂的一些恒星形成可能是沿着中心条发生的。如果得到证实，这种解释将改变天文学家理解银河系那部分恒星和气体排列的方式。

paras.en: New Evidence Could Redraw the Milky Way's Map
paras.zh: 新证据可以重新绘制银河系地图

paras.en: Beyond revealing an unusual location for star birth, the research also sheds light on the physical properties of the Galactic bar itself.
paras.zh: 除了揭示恒星诞生的不寻常地点之外，这项研究还揭示了银河棒本身的物理特性。

paras.en: Astronomers have debated the structure's length, orientation, and rotation speed for decades, partly because the Milky Way's dust and our viewing position make direct measurements so challenging.
paras.zh: 几十年来，天文学家一直在争论该结构的长度、方向和旋转速度，部分原因是银河系的尘埃和我们的观察位置使得直接测量变得非常具有挑战性。

paras.en: "Our findings place further constraints on the size, angle and rotation speed of this central bar," Dr. Davis said.
paras.zh: “我们的研究结果进一步限制了这个中心杆的尺寸、角度和旋转速度，”戴维斯博士说。

paras.en: The team's analysis indicates that the bar extends approximately 4.3 kiloparsecs, equivalent to about 14,000 light-years, outward from the galactic center along its long axis. This supports a picture of the Milky Way containing a relatively long bar that rotates slowly.
paras.zh: 研究小组的分析表明，该条带从银河系中心沿其长轴向外延伸约 4.3 千秒差距，相当于约 14,000 光年。这支持了银河系的图片，其中包含一条相对较长且缓慢旋转的条带。

paras.en: The results illustrate how increasingly sophisticated simulations can help scientists investigate regions of our galaxy that are difficult to observe directly. By comparing models spanning billions of years with the available astronomical evidence, researchers can narrow down the possible structures and processes shaping the Milky Way.
paras.zh: 结果表明，日益复杂的模拟如何帮助科学家研究银河系中难以直接观察的区域。通过将跨越数十亿年的模型与现有的天文学证据进行比较，研究人员可以缩小塑造银河系的可能结构和过程的范围。

paras.en: "By comparing a new generation of large-scale computerized galaxy simulations, evolving over billions of years, against a more limited set of observations, we now have a stronger understanding of the bar and star formation processes in the Milky Way," Dr. Davis said.
paras.zh: 戴维斯博士说：“通过将数十亿年演化的新一代大规模计算机星系模拟与一组更有限的观测进行比较，我们现在对银河系中的条形和恒星形成过程有了更深入的了解。”

paras.en: The authors reported no competing interests. Research funding came from the Australian Research Council, the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, the Swedish Research Council, the Swedish National Space Agency, the LMK Foundation and eSSENCE (Sweden).
paras.zh: 作者报告没有竞争利益。研究经费来自澳大利亚研究委员会、克努特和爱丽丝·瓦伦堡基金会、瑞典研究委员会、瑞典国家航天局、LMK 基金会和 eSSENCE（瑞典）。

paras.en: Computing resources and data storage were provided through National Computing Infrastructure Australia, an NCRIS capability supported by the Australian Government, and LUNARC, the Centre for Scientific and Technical Computing at Lund University, Sweden.
paras.zh: 计算资源和数据存储是通过澳大利亚国家计算基础设施（澳大利亚政府支持的 NCRIS 功能）和瑞典隆德大学科学技术计算中心 LUNARC 提供的。

paras.zh: 材料由悉尼大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.zh: - 希拉里·戴维斯、乔斯·布兰德·霍索恩、托尔·泰珀·加西亚、奥斯卡·阿格茨、伊丽莎白·J·艾尔斯。诺玛臂的本质是条形驱动的恒星形成激波锋。自然天文学，2026； DOI：10.1038/s41550-026-03010-5

articles.title: New gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good

paras.en: New gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good
paras.zh: 新的牙龈疾病治疗方法可以杀死坏细菌，同时保留好细菌

paras.en: Researchers in Japan have developed an innovative gum disease treatment that uses egg yolk antibodies and near-infrared light to destroy harmful bacteria without harming beneficial microbes. Unlike conventional treatments, the approach preserves the mouth's natural bacterial balance and protects healthy gum cells. In mice, it significantly reduced the bone loss associated with periodontitis, a major cause of tooth loss.
paras.zh: 日本研究人员开发了一种创新的牙龈疾病治疗方法，利用蛋黄抗体和近红外光来消灭有害细菌，而不伤害有益微生物。与传统治疗不同，该方法可以保持口腔的自然细菌平衡并保护健康的牙龈细胞。在小鼠中，它显着减少了与牙周炎相关的骨质流失，牙周炎是牙齿脱落的主要原因。

paras.en: Researchers in Japan have developed a promising new treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed. Unlike conventional approaches that can eliminate both good and bad bacteria, the new therapy is designed to target specific microbes responsible for damaging gums and the bone that supports teeth.
paras.zh: 日本研究人员开发出了一种很有前途的牙龈疾病新疗法，可以杀死有害细菌，同时使有益微生物不受伤害。与可以消除好细菌和坏细菌的传统方法不同，新疗法旨在针对破坏牙龈和支撑牙齿的骨骼的特定微生物。

paras.en: Developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light. Early experiments in human cell cultures and mice suggest that it could offer a more precise way to combat periodontitis, a serious form of gum disease that can eventually lead to tooth loss. The findings were published in the Journal of Translational Medicine.
paras.zh: 该疗法由名古屋大学的科学家开发，将从蛋黄中获得的抗体与近红外光相结合。人类细胞培养物和小鼠的早期实验表明，它可以提供一种更精确的方法来对抗牙周炎，牙周炎是一种严重的牙龈疾病，最终会导致牙齿脱落。研究结果发表在《转化医学杂志》上。

paras.en: Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems
paras.zh: 为什么传统牙龈疾病治疗会引起问题

paras.en: The human mouth contains a complex community of microorganisms, many of which play important roles in maintaining oral health. Problems can arise when harmful bacteria multiply and disturb this delicate balance.
paras.zh: 人类口腔含有复杂的微生物群落，其中许多微生物在维持口腔健康方面发挥着重要作用。当有害细菌繁殖并破坏这种微妙的平衡时，就会出现问题。

paras.en: One particularly troublesome species is Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis), which scientists classify as a keystone pathogen. This means it can have an outsized influence on the surrounding microbial community, even when it is not especially abundant. By promoting inflammation and disrupting the normal balance of oral bacteria, it can contribute to the destruction of the bone that holds teeth in place.
paras.zh: 牙龈卟啉单胞菌（P. gingivalis）是一个特别麻烦的物种，科学家将其归类为关键病原体。这意味着它可以对周围的微生物群落产生巨大的影响，即使它不是特别丰富。通过促进炎症和破坏口腔细菌的正常平衡，它可能会破坏固定牙齿的骨骼。

paras.en: Treating periodontitis often involves eliminating the bacteria responsible for the infection. However, some existing antimicrobial treatments do not distinguish between harmful organisms and microbes that help maintain a healthy mouth.
paras.zh: 治疗牙周炎通常涉及消除引起感染的细菌。然而，一些现有的抗菌治疗无法区分有害生物体和有助于保持口腔健康的微生物。

paras.en: "Current treatments for periodontitis, including antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT), eliminate both pathogenic and beneficial oral bacteria," said Kazuhide Sato, one of the corresponding authors and a lecturer at Nagoya University. "These approaches often disrupt the entire oral microbial ecosystem and can also release lipopolysaccharide (LPS), an endotoxin that may exacerbate inflammation."
paras.zh: “目前牙周炎的治疗方法，包括抗生素和抗菌光动力疗法（aPDT），可以消除致病性和有益的口腔细菌，”通讯作者之一、名古屋大学讲师 Kazuhide Sato 说。 “这些方法通常会破坏整个口腔微生物生态系统，还会释放脂多糖（LPS），这是一种可能加剧炎症的内毒素。”

paras.en: Scientists Adapt Cancer Therapy to Target Gum Disease Bacteria
paras.zh: 科学家采用癌症疗法来针对牙龈疾病细菌

paras.en: To overcome these limitations, the Nagoya University team turned to a technology originally designed to treat cancer. Known as near-infrared photoimmunotherapy, it uses antibodies linked to a light-sensitive dye to recognize specific targets. Once the compound attaches to its intended target, exposure to near-infrared light activates the dye and produces a damaging effect.
paras.zh: 为了克服这些限制，名古屋大学团队转向了一种最初设计用于治疗癌症的技术。它被称为近红外光免疫疗法，使用与光敏染料连接的抗体来识别特定目标。一旦化合物附着到其预期目标上，暴露于近红外光下就会激活染料并产生破坏性效果。

paras.en: The researchers adapted this strategy to attack P. gingivalis without unnecessarily disturbing other oral bacteria. Their approach relies on IgY, a type of antibody collected from the egg yolks of hens that have been immunized against the pathogen.
paras.zh: 研究人员采用了这种策略来攻击牙龈卟啉单胞菌，而不会不必要地干扰其他口腔细菌。他们的方法依赖于 IgY，这是一种从已针对病原体免疫的母鸡蛋黄中收集的抗体。

paras.en: Egg yolk antibodies offer a practical advantage because they can be produced in large quantities at relatively low cost. This could make them an attractive option for developing targeted treatments that are affordable and scalable.
paras.zh: 蛋黄抗体具有实际优势，因为它们可以以相对较低的成本大量生产。这可能使它们成为开发负担得起且可扩展的针对性治疗方法的有吸引力的选择。

paras.en: The resulting technology, called near-infrared photo-antibacterial targeting therapy (NIR-PAT²), was developed by researchers at Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine. The team included first author Hiroshi Maruyama, Professor Hideharu Hibi, and corresponding authors Sato and Kiyoshi Sakai.
paras.zh: 由此产生的技术被称为近红外光抗菌靶向治疗（NIR-PAT²），由名古屋大学医学研究生院的研究人员开发。该团队包括第一作者 Hiroshi Maruyama、Hideharu Hibi 教授以及通讯作者 Sato 和 Kiyoshi Sakai。

paras.en: To determine whether the treatment could destroy harmful bacteria while protecting healthy tissue, the researchers tested it in human cell cultures and mice. They also compared its effects with those of conventional antimicrobial therapies.
paras.zh: 为了确定这种治疗方法是否可以消灭有害细菌，同时保护健康组织，研究人员在人类细胞培养物和小鼠中进行了测试。他们还将其效果与传统抗菌疗法进行了比较。

paras.en: Light-Activated Antibodies Destroy Harmful Bacteria
paras.zh: 光激活抗体消灭有害细菌

paras.en: Laboratory experiments showed that the antibody and dye combination attached specifically to P. gingivalis. Other bacterial species and healthy human gum cells were left unaffected.
paras.zh: 实验室实验表明，抗体和染料组合特异​​性附着于牙龈卟啉单胞菌。其他细菌种类和健康的人类牙龈细胞不受影响。

paras.en: When the researchers illuminated the targeted bacteria with near-infrared light, the activated dye damaged their outer membranes, ultimately killing them.
paras.zh: 当研究人员用近红外光照射目标细菌时，活化的染料会损坏它们的外膜，最终杀死它们。

paras.en: Microscopic examination revealed an important difference between this technique and conventional antimicrobial light therapy. Bacteria exposed to the new treatment developed tiny openings in their membranes but largely maintained their overall shape. By contrast, conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy caused the bacteria to break apart completely.
paras.zh: 显微镜检查揭示了该技术与传统抗菌光疗法之间的重要区别。接受新处理的细菌在其膜上形成了微小的开口，但基本上保持了其整体形状。相比之下，传统的抗菌光动力疗法导致细菌完全分解。

paras.en: The distinction matters because destroying bacterial cells can release substances that contribute to inflammation. Preserving the overall structure of the targeted bacteria, even after killing them, could help limit this unwanted effect.
paras.zh: 这种区别很重要，因为破坏细菌细胞会释放导致炎症的物质。保留目标细菌的整体结构，即使在杀死它们之后，也有助于限制这种不良影响。

paras.en: The researchers also examined how the treatments affected healthy human gum cells. Their targeted therapy caused no detectable harm to these cells, while conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy produced cellular damage and slowed healing.
paras.zh: 研究人员还研究了这些治疗如何影响健康的人类牙龈细胞。他们的靶向治疗对这些细胞没有造成可检测到的伤害，而传统的抗菌光动力疗法会造成细胞损伤并减慢愈合速度。

paras.en: The team next investigated whether these laboratory findings would translate into meaningful improvements in gum disease.
paras.zh: 研究小组接下来调查了这些实验室研究结果是否会转化为牙龈疾病的有意义的改善。

paras.en: In mice with periodontitis, the experimental therapy significantly reduced the loss of alveolar bone, the part of the jawbone that surrounds and supports teeth. Preventing this type of bone deterioration is especially important because advanced periodontitis can loosen teeth and eventually cause them to fall out.
paras.zh: 在患有牙周炎的小鼠中，实验疗法显着减少了牙槽骨的损失，牙槽骨是颌骨中包围和支撑牙齿的部分。防止这种类型的骨质退化尤其重要，因为晚期牙周炎会使牙齿松动并最终导致牙齿脱落。

paras.en: Analysis of the animals' saliva revealed another encouraging result. The treatment reduced P. gingivalis while preserving beneficial Streptococcus bacteria, helping maintain a healthier balance of microorganisms in the mouth.
paras.zh: 对动物唾液的分析揭示了另一个令人鼓舞的结果。该治疗减少了牙龈卟啉单胞菌，同时保留了有益的链球菌，有助于维持口腔微生物的健康平衡。

paras.en: Conventional antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, on the other hand, eliminated both harmful and beneficial bacteria in the experiments, causing broader disruption to the oral microbial community.
paras.zh: 另一方面，传统抗生素和抗菌光动力疗法在实验中消除了有害和有益细菌，对口腔微生物群落造成更广泛的破坏。

paras.en: "Results demonstrated that, unlike antibiotics or standard light therapy, this approach selectively removes the primary pathogenic species while preserving the remainder of the oral bacterial community," Sato said.
paras.zh: 佐藤说：“结果表明，与抗生素或标准光疗法不同，这种方法选择性地去除主要致病菌，同时保留口腔细菌群落的其余部分。”

paras.en: Together, the findings suggest that targeting individual disease-causing bacteria could help control gum disease while avoiding some of the unintended consequences of broader antimicrobial treatments.
paras.zh: 总之，研究结果表明，针对个别致病细菌可以帮助控制牙龈疾病，同时避免更广泛的抗菌治疗带来的一些意想不到的后果。

paras.en: AI Could Help Develop More Precise Gum Disease Treatments
paras.zh: 人工智能可以帮助开发更精确的牙龈疾病治疗方法

paras.en: Although the early results are promising, the researchers recognize that periodontitis is a complex disease involving multiple bacterial species. Eliminating P. gingivalis alone may not be sufficient to treat every case.
paras.zh: 尽管早期结果令人鼓舞，但研究人员认识到牙周炎是一种涉及多种细菌的复杂疾病。仅消除牙龈卟啉单胞菌可能不足以治疗所有病例。

paras.en: To address this challenge, the team plans to use artificial intelligence (AI) to examine publicly available information about oral bacteria. By identifying other important microorganisms and studying how different species interact, they hope to uncover additional targets for future therapies.
paras.zh: 为了应对这一挑战，该团队计划使用人工智能（AI）来检查有关口腔细菌的公开信息。通过识别其他重要的微生物并研究不同物种如何相互作用，他们希望发现未来治疗的更多靶点。

paras.en: The researchers also see potential implications beyond oral health. Periodontitis has been linked to several other medical conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and diabetes.
paras.zh: 研究人员还看到了口腔健康之外的潜在影响。牙周炎与其他几种疾病有关，包括类风湿性关节炎和糖尿病。

paras.en: Understanding the relationships between oral bacteria and these conditions could eventually help scientists identify which patients are most likely to benefit from specific treatments. AI analysis may play a role in making those decisions and guiding the development of more personalized approaches to gum disease.
paras.zh: 了解口腔细菌与这些疾病之间的关系最终可以帮助科学家确定哪些患者最有可能从特定治疗中受益。人工智能分析可能在做出这些决策和指导开发更个性化的牙龈疾病方法方面发挥作用。

paras.en: For now, the therapy remains experimental, with its effectiveness demonstrated in laboratory studies and mice rather than human clinical trials. However, the findings point toward a possible future in which treating gum disease means selectively removing harmful bacteria instead of disrupting the entire microbial community that helps keep the mouth healthy.
paras.zh: 目前，该疗法仍处于实验阶段，其有效性是在实验室研究和小鼠而非人体临床试验中得到证明的。然而，研究结果指出了一个可能的未来：治疗牙龈疾病意味着选择性地去除有害细菌，而不是破坏有助于保持口腔健康的整个微生物群落。

paras.en: Materials provided by Nagoya University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 资料由名古屋大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Hiroshi Maruyama, Kazuhide Sato, Kiyoshi Sakai, Hirotoshi Yasui, Ryu Okada, Li Xinheng, Koji Umeda, Shofiqur Rahman, Van Sa Nguyen, Hideharu Hibi. Near infrared photo-bacterialflora modulation technology realized controlling periodontitis: modulation of disease-associated dysbiosis in oral microbiota using near infrared photo-antibacterial targeting therapy (NIR-PAT2). Journal of Translational Medicine, 2026; 24 (1) DOI: 10.1186/s12967-026-08336-2

articles.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work
articles.author: Alan Bradley

paras.en: Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics. The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation, the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut.
paras.zh: 太空运动有着悠久而光荣的传统，无论是艾伦·谢泼德在月球上打高尔夫球，还是国际空间站的工作人员举办自己的夏季奥运会。随着太空运动联合会的成立，未来看起来也很光明，该联合会自称为“第一个零重力或微重力竞技运动的管理和制裁机构”，由美国宇航局宇航员共同创立。

paras.en: Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field.
paras.zh: 科幻小说也不甘示弱，将零重力和低重力运动的理念扩展到了逻辑范围，想象了从《神秘博士》的零重力壁球到《安德的游戏》先进的游戏化战斗模拟。甚至还有太空大灌篮的外星篮球比赛，以决定地球的命运，尽管其中的反重力滑稽动作来自卡通恶作剧，而不是零重力的比赛场地。

paras.en: As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play.
paras.zh: 随着人类通过阿尔忒弥斯计划等项目及其在月球上建立栖息地的雄心，逐渐接近殖民我们的邻居，我们的想象力必须扩大，不仅包括我们如何在太空生活，还包括我们如何玩耍。

paras.en: The rules change when gravity disappears
paras.zh: 当重力消失时规则就会改变

paras.en: We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. It defines how balls arc, how quickly players can move, and even how we orient ourselves in play spaces. Remove the gravity, and all of those assumptions and mechanics evaporate as well.
paras.zh: 我们很少在地球背景下思考这个问题，但每项运动都受到重力的严重影响。它定义了球的弧线、球员移动的速度，甚至我们在比赛空间中如何定位自己。除去重力，所有这些假设和力学也会消失。

paras.en: "First of all, in zero g, Isaac Newton will win every time," Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, told Space. Les is a physicist with over 35 years of experience working at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, as well as a science fiction author.
paras.zh: “首先，在零重力下，艾萨克·牛顿每次都会获胜，”美国宇航局前首席技术专家莱斯·约翰逊告诉《太空》杂志。 Les 是一位物理学家，在阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔的马歇尔太空飞行中心拥有超过 35 年的工作经验，同时也是一位科幻小说作家。

paras.en: "'For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,'" quotes Johnson. "This is very difficult to simulate in real life due to gravity; special effects often try to compensate. With today’s AI and green screens, it can actually look good on screen."
paras.zh: “‘对于每一个行动，都会产生相同且相反的反应，’”约翰逊引用道。 “由于重力的原因，这在现实生活中很难模拟；特效通常会尝试弥补。借助当今的人工智能和绿屏，它实际上可以在屏幕上看起来不错。”

paras.en: In a microgravity scenario, the concept of up and down is no longer relevant. Suddenly, the playing field expands from a single, fixed plane to a fully three-dimensional space that includes height.
paras.zh: 在微重力场景中，上下的概念不再相关。突然，比赛场地从一个固定的平面扩展到一个包含高度的完整三维空间。

paras.en: Momentum is also a completely different beast. Instead of being able to quickly stop and pivot the way you can during terrestrial sports, once you start moving in microgravity, you keep going until something stops you. It takes the trickiness of moving on ice in sports like hockey and increases it by several orders of magnitude.
paras.zh: 动量也是一种完全不同的野兽。一旦你开始在微重力中移动，你就会继续前进，直到有东西阻止你为止，而不是像陆地运动中那样快速停止和旋转。它消除了曲棍球等运动中在冰上移动的技巧，并将其提高了几个数量级。

paras.en: Of course, the havoc wouldn't stop with maneuvering yourself. Any ball or other object would also be subject to this altered set of physics.
paras.zh: 当然，破坏不会因为你自己的操纵而停止。任何球或其他物体也将受到这套改变的物理原理的影响。

paras.en: As Johnson points out, "Aside from maneuvering the body and not tumbling or going in the wrong direction, the most difficult part would probably be throwing or hitting a ball in zero g. There would be no arc, just a straight-line throw. That would take getting used to doing, given that we’ve spent our entire lives calculating how high and fast to throw a ball in 1G so it gets to the person we intend."
paras.zh: 正如约翰逊指出的那样，“除了操纵身体、不翻滚或走错方向之外，最困难的部分可能是在零重力下投掷或击球。不会有弧线，只有直线投掷。这需要习惯，因为我们一生都在计算在 1G 下投掷球的高度和速度，以便它到达我们想要的人。”

paras.en: Science fiction interpretations have often leaned into these differences; in many cases, low-g sports look more like three-dimensional chess than the highly physical contests we're used to here on Earth.
paras.zh: 科幻小说的解释常常倾向于这些差异。在许多情况下，低重力运动看起来更像三维国际象棋，而不是我们在地球上习惯的高强度竞赛。

paras.en: Ironically, many of the best examples of space-based sports are the most grounded, where real-world physics are fully accounted for.
paras.zh: 讽刺的是，许多太空运动的最佳例子都是最接地气的，充分考虑了现实世界的物理学。

paras.en: 2013's "Ender's Game" gives us one of the best examples of a zero-g arena in space. Dubbed the "Battle Room," it's a giant hollow cube filled with obstacles. Teams enter through gates at opposite ends and participate in laser tag-style drills while having to grapple with three-dimensional space, while also finding ways to propel and protect themselves.
paras.zh: 2013 年的《安德的游戏》为我们提供了太空零重力竞技场的最佳示例之一。它被称为“战斗室”，是一个充满障碍的巨大空心立方体。团队从两端的大门进入，参加激光标签式的演习，同时必须应对三维空间，同时还要找到推动和保护自己的方法。

paras.en: "The Battle Room sequence does a great job of thinking about straight‑line, constant‑velocity motion," Johnson said. "No 'reaction' to slow you down or change your direction. Characters push off walls or each other, then drift until they hit something or fire their suit's thrusters."
paras.zh: “战斗室序列在考虑直线、恒速运动方面做得很好，”约翰逊说。 “没有‘反应’来减慢你的速度或改变你的方向。角色会推开墙壁或互相推开，然后漂移，直到撞到某物或发射宇航服的推进器。”

paras.en: Johnson said Ender's Game also did an admirable job of showcasing how alternate physics require another layer of planning when moving through space.
paras.zh: 约翰逊表示，《安德的游戏》也做了一项令人钦佩的工作，展示了替代物理在穿越太空时如何需要另一层规划。

paras.en: "They went to great lengths to show that there was no preferred 'up' or 'down'. Again, very accurate and realistic thinking. Floating obstacles in the battle space created realistic constraints: if you don't think about where you'll rebound, you can pin yourself behind an obstacle or drift out of the fight."
paras.zh: “他们不遗余力地表明，没有‘上’或‘下’之分。同样，这是非常准确和现实的思维。战斗空间中漂浮的障碍物造成了现实的限制：如果你不考虑你会在哪里反弹，你可能会把自己固定在障碍物后面或偏离战斗。”

paras.en: Recognizing how important play can be (and, perhaps, acknowledging ways to combat the lingering specter of space madness), real-world space agencies have begun brainstorming what recreation in low gravity might look like. Some proposed ideas include 3D ball games not wholly dissimilar from the Battle Room, where players enter a cube or spherical arena and push off walls/pass a ball in any direction, scoring by hitting targets.
paras.zh: 认识到游戏的重要性（也许还认识到对抗挥之不去的太空疯狂幽灵的方法），现实世界的太空机构已经开始集思广益，讨论低重力下的娱乐可能是什么样子。一些提出的想法包括与战斗室没有完全不同的 3D 球类游戏，玩家进入一个立方体或球形竞技场并推开墙壁/向任何方向传球，通过击中目标得分。

paras.en: Elastic tethers are another experimental concept being bandied around, where players are connected to flexible tethers to improve movement control and cut down on collisions. The Space Games Federation has also floated the idea of a version of space basketball, where the goal is guiding a magnetic ball through hoops, as well as some version of space dodgeball.
paras.zh: 弹性系绳是另一个正在广泛使用的实验性概念，玩家可以连接到灵活的系绳上，以改善运动控制并减少碰撞。太空运动联合会还提出了太空篮球的想法，其目标是引导磁球穿过篮筐，以及某种版本的太空躲避球。

paras.en: Of course, these proposals are nothing more than thought exercises at the moment. We're a long way out from vast human populations living in zero-g environments for extended periods of time, and even further still from building spaceships capable of housing a sports hall.
paras.zh: 当然，目前这些建议只不过是思想练习。我们距离大量人口长期生活在零重力环境中还有很长的路要走，距离建造能够容纳体育馆的宇宙飞船更远。

paras.en: NASA astronauts have experimented with trying to play various terrestrial sports in space, usually aboard the International Space Station. We've seen them playing soccer, lacrosse, and hockey with varying degrees of success.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局宇航员尝试在太空中进行各种地面运动，通常是在国际空间站上。我们看到他们在踢足球、长曲棍球和曲棍球方面取得了不同程度的成功。

paras.en: These fun experiments mainly serve to prove what we've already suspected: that terrestrial sports can't be directly translated into a zero-g environment. We'll need new rules, arenas, and whole new games if we're going to make any headway with competitive sports in space.
paras.zh: 这些有趣的实验主要是为了证明我们已经怀疑的事情：陆地运动不能直接转化为零重力环境。如果我们想在太空竞技运动方面取得任何进展，我们就需要新的规则、竞技场和全新的游戏。

paras.en: Where sci‑fi gets it right (and wrong) about space sports
paras.zh: 科幻小说中关于太空运动的正确（和错误）之处

paras.en: Sci-fi has a pretty good track record for simulating open 3D environments in microgravity. The genre also tends to do fairly well in depicting the methodical pace of moving through space and how that would affect competition (and combat).
paras.zh: 科幻小说在模拟微重力下的开放 3D 环境方面有着良好的记录。该类型在描绘太空移动的有条不紊的节奏以及这将如何影响竞争（和战斗）方面也往往表现得相当好。

paras.en: Games like "Echo Arena" even use technology to help simulate these factors. Echo Arena is a VR game where you boost around a zero-g arena, punching opponents and trying to toss a disc into a goal.
paras.zh: 像《Echo Arena》这样的游戏甚至使用技术来帮助模拟这些因素。 Echo Arena 是一款 VR 游戏，您可以在零重力竞技场中加速，猛击对手并尝试将圆盘扔进球门。

paras.en: The game's innovative movement system allows players to grab almost any surface, either moving themselves along it or pushing off to float in a given direction. Players are also given wrist-mounted thrusters to let them course-correct a little, offering a respite from the unforgiving laws of motion.
paras.zh: 游戏的创新移动系统允许玩家抓住几乎任何表面，要么沿着它移动自己，要么沿着给定方向推动漂浮。玩家还配备了安装在手腕上的推进器，让他们稍微修正一下航向，让他们暂时摆脱无情的运动法则。

paras.en: Dead Space also has a section that functions similarly but with conventional game controls, though the only sport there is "don't get eaten by necromorphs."
paras.zh: 《死亡空间》也有一个功能类似的部分，但采用传统的游戏控制，尽管那里唯一的运动是“不要被死灵吃掉”。

paras.en: With that said, there are areas where sci-fi portrayals of zero-G games fall down. Energy levels and fatigue is a big one: constant maneuvering with your arms is exhausting, which is why real astronauts rely heavily on handholds. In a similar vein, there's the issue of infinite momentum, specifically as it applies to rotation.
paras.zh: 话虽如此，零重力游戏的科幻形象在某些方面是失败的。能量水平和疲劳是一个很大的问题：不断地用手臂进行操纵会让人筋疲力尽，这就是为什么真正的宇航员严重依赖扶手的原因。同样，存在无限动量的问题，特别是当它适用于旋转时。

paras.en: Johnson specifically quibbles with scenes in the Ender's Game Battle Room and "how quickly the participants can rotate their bodies or part of their bodies without going into an uncontrollable spin." He points to incidents where real-life astronauts have demonstrated how challenging this phenomenon would actually be. "I’ve watched many videos of astronauts on the ISS twist and then bounce off the wall or something. They have all looked very clumsy when they do this."
paras.zh: 约翰逊特别对安德游戏战斗室中的场景以及“参与者能够以多快的速度旋转他们的身体或身体的一部分而不会陷入无法控制的旋转”提出了质疑。他指出，现实生活中的宇航员已经证明了这种现象实际上是多么具有挑战性。 “我看过很多宇航员在国际空间站上扭转然后从墙壁或其他东西上弹起的视频。他们这样做时看起来都非常笨拙。”

paras.en: The other kind of space constraints are also often hand-waved. Even the largest existing spacecraft pale in comparison to the size of stadiums or arenas on Earth. Our early attempts at space-based sports will likely have to be centered in much smaller playing areas.
paras.zh: 另一种空间限制也经常被挥手。与地球上体育场或竞技场的大小相比，即使是现有最大的航天器也相形见绌。我们对太空运动的早期尝试可能必须集中在较小的比赛区域。

paras.en: Safety issues are frequently downplayed as well; colliding with metal surfaces at high speeds in enclosed environments risks serious bodily harm to players as well as potential damage to suits/gear.
paras.zh: 安全问题也经常被淡化。在封闭环境中高速与金属表面碰撞可能会对玩家造成严重的身体伤害，并可能对服装/装备造成损坏。

paras.en: With that said, newer sci-fi portrayals are getting closer to reality by emphasizing slower, more deliberate movement and placing the focus on strategic thinking rather than athletic prowess.
paras.zh: 话虽如此，新的科幻形象通过强调更慢、更从容的动作，并将重点放在战略思维而不是运动能力上，越来越接近现实。

paras.en: In the meantime, astronauts might have to stick to video games to scratch their competitive itches.
paras.zh: 与此同时，宇航员可能不得不坚持玩电子游戏来满足他们的竞争欲望。

paras.en: Alan Bradley is an experienced tech and culture writer with more than 20 years covering gaming, tech, and hardware. His work has appeared in Rolling Stone, U.S. News & World Report, PCMag, TechRadar, GamesRadar+, CNET, Live Science, Variety, and many other outlets.
paras.zh: Alan Bradley 是一位经验丰富的科技和文化作家，拥有 20 多年的游戏、科技和硬件领域经验。他的作品曾出现在《滚石》、《美国新闻与世界报道》、PCMag、TechRadar、GamesRadar+、CNET、Live Science、Variety 和许多其他媒体上。

articles.title: Join our free Space.com membership giveaway for a chance to win this Dwarflab mini smart telescope worth $419!
articles.author: Tariq Malik

paras.en: Hey, Space Fans! Our Space.com Community team has launched a new giveaway exclusively for our Space+ members, and you can join for free now for a chance to win one of two Dwarflab mini smart telescopes, each worth $419.
paras.zh: 嘿，太空迷们！我们的 Space.com 社区团队专门为 Space+ 会员推出了一项新赠品，您现在可以免费加入，有机会赢得两台 Dwarflab 迷你智能望远镜之一，每台价值 419 美元。

paras.en: Already a Space+ member (hey, thanks!), you can still enter by entering the email associated with your membership on the entry page.
paras.zh: 已经是 Space+ 会员（嘿，谢谢！），您仍然可以通过在输入页面上输入与您的会员资格相关的电子邮件来输入。

paras.en: While this Dwarflab smart telescope giveaway is our first contest, it won't be the last. Keep in mind, your entry is for a chance to win one of the two telescopes and there will be two U.S. winners in all.
paras.zh: 虽然这次 Dwarflab 智能望远镜赠品是我们的第一次竞赛，但它不会是最后一次。请记住，您的参与是有机会赢得两台望远镜中的一台，总共将有两台美国获胜者。

paras.en: If you're curious about why we picked Dwarflab's portable telescopes as a prize, check out our Dwarflab Mini smart telescope review to learn more.
paras.zh: 如果您好奇为什么我们选择 Dwarflab 便携式望远镜作为奖品，请查看我们的 Dwarflab 迷你智能望远镜评论以了解更多信息。

paras.en: We found the ultra-compact 30-mm refractor telescope to be one of the most portable smart telescopes around, and an affordable entry-level option for stargazers hoping to break into smart telescope astrophotography on a budget.
paras.zh: 我们发现超紧凑型 30 毫米折射望远镜是最便携的智能望远镜之一，对于希望在预算内进入智能望远镜天文摄影领域的观星者来说，这是一个经济实惠的入门级选择。

paras.en: So if you're new to our Space+ crew, welcome aboard, and if you're a returning member entering the Dwarflab drawing, good luck!
paras.zh: 因此，如果您是我们 Space+ 团队的新成员，欢迎加入，如果您是进入 Dwarflab 绘图的回归成员，祝您好运！

paras.en: We'll announce the winners in January 2027 via our contest page.
paras.zh: 我们将在 2027 年 1 月通过我们的竞赛页面宣布获奖者。

paras.en: Tariq is the award-winning Editor-in-Chief of Space.com and joined the team in 2001. He covers human spaceflight, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Editor-in-Chief in 2019. Before joining Space.com, Tariq was a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra, Fullerton and Huntington Beach. He's a recipient of the 2022 Harry Kolcum Award for excellence in space reporting and the 2025 Space Pioneer Award from the National Space Society. He is an Eagle Scout and Space Camp alum with journalism degrees from the USC and NYU. You can find Tariq at Space.com and as the co-host to the This Week In Space podcast on the TWiT network. To see his latest project, you can follow Tariq on Twitter @tariqjmalik.
paras.zh: Tariq 是 Space.com 屡获殊荣的主编，于 2001 年加入该团队。他负责载人航天以及天空观测和娱乐。他于 2019 年成为 Space.com 的主编。在加入 Space.com 之前，塔里克是《洛杉矶时报》的特约记者，报道拉哈布拉、富勒顿和亨廷顿海滩的教育和城市动态。他因其在太空报道方面的卓越表现而荣获 2022 年哈利·科尔库姆奖和国家航天协会颁发的 2025 年太空先锋奖。他是鹰童子军和太空营的校友，拥有南加州大学和纽约大学的新闻学学位。您可以在 Space.com 上找到塔里克，他也是 TWiT 网络上本周太空播客的联合主持人。要查看他的最新项目，您可以在 Twitter 上关注 Tariq @tariqjmalik。

articles.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
articles.author: Julian Dossett

paras.en: It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局正在努力实现在月球上的永久存在，这已不是什么秘密。该航天局甚至计划建造一个月球基地，供宇航员回家。但全天候生活在月球栖息地的人类每天需要三餐，因此研究人员一直在研究如何在月球上种植食物。

paras.en: To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal.
paras.zh: 为此，俄勒冈州立大学农业科学学院的一个团队一直在模拟月球尘埃中种植土豆，并取得了可喜的成果。研究人员于 11 月 20 日在《微重力科学》杂志上发表了他们的发现。

paras.en: "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement. "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon."
paras.zh: 俄勒冈州立大学植物学和植物病理学系副教授艾默里克·戈耶在一份声明中说：“我们发现，补充有机物后，土豆可以在模拟月球土壤中完成其整个生命周期。” “这是朝着开发可靠的粮食生产系统迈出的重要一步，该系统可以支持人类对月球的长期探索。”

paras.en: To grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith, the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions.
paras.zh: 为了培育土豆，科学家们使用了五种不同的材料，这些材料类似于覆盖月球表面的风化层、灰尘和岩石。月球包含具有独特表面构成的各个区域，因此他们使用的材料模拟了来自月海和月球高地地区的风化层。

paras.en: The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil.
paras.zh: 秘密成分是蚯蚓堆肥，这是一种富含营养的土壤。研究小组在模拟风化层中添加了不同程度的蚯蚓堆肥来种植土豆。他们发现，将假风化土与 30% 的蚯蚓堆肥混合，其效果与在普通土壤中种植土豆的效果相当。

paras.en: "We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement.
paras.zh: 戈耶实验室的博士后研究员戴维·汉迪（David Handy）在同一份声明中表示：“我们相信，堆肥可以通过减少植物接触有害化合物来平衡我们在月球风化层中看到的一些毒性。”

paras.en: The idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth.
paras.zh: 这个想法是，未来的宇航员可以携带一些营养丰富的土壤，并将其与风化层混合来种植土豆。毕竟，从地球运送所有食物需要花费大量成本。

paras.en: Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

articles.title: NASA+ Documentary Captures Europa Clipper’s Journey Into Deep Space
articles.author: Amanda Barnett

paras.en: NASA invites the world behind the scenes to witness the story of Europa Clipper’s journey from a far-off vision to a cutting-edge deep space exploration mission with the release of the agency’s newest documentary, “The Europa Concept.”
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 发布最新纪录片《欧罗巴概念》，邀请幕后世界见证欧罗巴快艇从遥远愿景到尖端深空探索任务的旅程故事。

paras.en: The documentary will air on NASA+, the NASA app, and the agency’s website starting Monday, Nov. 23, and is coming soon to YouTube.
paras.zh: 这部纪录片将于 11 月 23 日星期一开始在 NASA+、NASA 应用程序和该机构的网站上播出，并将很快在 YouTube 上推出。

paras.en: It took decades of science, thousands of dedicated minds, endless creativity, and a whole lot of grit to get the Europa Clipper spacecraft to the launch pad in 2024. Now the orbiter, the largest NASA has ever sent into deep space, is two years into its five-year, 1.8 billion-mile (2.9 billion-kilometer) journey to the Jupiter system, where it will conduct flybys of Europa in search of the conditions for life in the vast ocean thought to hide beneath the moon’s icy surface.
paras.zh: 经过数十年的科学努力、数千名专注的头脑、无尽的创造力和巨大的毅力，欧罗巴快艇航天器于 2024 年抵达发射台。现在，这艘轨道器是 NASA 有史以来发射到深空的最大的轨道飞行器，其为期 5 年、18 亿英里（29 亿公里）的木星系统之旅已进入两年，它将飞越木星系统，在被认为隐藏在木星下方的广阔海洋中寻找生命的条件。月球冰冷的表面。

paras.en: “The things we will learn from Europa Clipper will be so sensational, so fantastic, that everyone will be screaming for the next mission,” said Curt Niebur, program scientist in the Planetary Science Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. “The only thing that matters is that we learn enough that we, in the broadest sense, want to do it again somewhere else — because that’s what exploration is.”
paras.zh: 美国宇航局华盛顿总部行星科学部的项目科学家科特·尼布尔说：“我们将从欧罗巴快船学到的东西将是如此轰动、如此奇妙，以至于每个人都会为下一次任务而尖叫。” “唯一重要的是，我们学到了足够多的东西，从最广泛的意义上来说，我们想在其他地方再次这样做——因为这就是探索。”

paras.en: Following a team of dedicated engineers and scientists on their yearslong efforts, the documentary captures how they developed a mission to Europa and built a spacecraft capable of surviving one of the most punishing radiation environments in our solar system. A product of Jupiter’s powerful magnetic field, that same radiation may have contributed to creating a potentially habitable environment on Europa.
paras.zh: 这部纪录片讲述了一群敬业的工程师和科学家经过多年的努力，记录了他们如何制定欧罗巴任务并建造一艘能够在太阳系最恶劣的辐射环境之一中生存的航天器。作为木星强大磁场的产物，同样的辐射可能有助于在木卫二上创造一个潜在的宜居环境。

paras.en: The moon, an object of fascination since its discovery by Galileo Galilei in 1610, only began to reveal its secrets with data obtained by NASA’s Pioneer 10 in 1973, followed the next year by Pioneer 11. But humanity didn’t get its first detailed look at Europa until Voyager 1’s flyby in 1979. More detailed glimpses of the moon followed from the agency’s Voyager 2, Galileo, Cassini, and Juno missions, each helping illuminate the way for Europa Clipper.
paras.zh: 自伽利略·伽利雷于 1610 年发现月球以来，月球一直是一个令人着迷的物体，直到 1973 年美国宇航局先锋 10 号和次年先锋 11 号获得的数据才开始揭示它的秘密。但直到 1979 年航海家 1 号飞越木卫二时，人类才第一次详细观察木卫二。随后该机构的航海家 2 号对月球进行了更详细的观察。伽利略号、卡西尼号和朱诺号任务，每一个都帮助照亮了欧罗巴快艇的道路。

paras.en: Work officially began on the mission at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California in 2013, initiating an 11-year trek to build the spacecraft and its suite of nine science instruments in time to launch during a specific period of planetary alignment. Along the way, the team encountered plenty of unforeseen challenges, including a global pandemic and, just before launch on Oct. 14, 2024, a Category 5 hurricane and tornadoes near NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
paras.zh: 2013 年，这项任务的工作在美国宇航局南加州喷气推进实验室正式开始，开始了为期 11 年的艰苦跋涉，建造航天器及其九套科学仪器，以便在特定的行星排列期间及时发射。在此过程中，该团队遇到了许多不可预见的挑战，包括全球大流行，以及在 2024 年 10 月 14 日发射之前，佛罗里达州 NASA 肯尼迪航天中心附近发生的 5 级飓风和龙卷风。

paras.en: “With Europa Clipper, we’ve taken the next step in solar system exploration, which will help us uncover the mysteries of an ocean world, and ultimately, whether potentially habitable worlds beyond our own exist,” said Jordan Evans, director of flight projects at JPL and the mission’s previous project manager. “This documentary pays tribute to the ingenuity, teamwork, and dedication that continue to make this incredible mission possible.”
paras.zh: 喷气推进实验室飞行项目总监、该任务的前项目经理乔丹·埃文斯 (Jordan Evans) 表示：“通过欧罗巴快船，我们在太阳系探索方面迈出了下一步，这将帮助我们揭开海洋世界的奥秘，并最终帮助我们揭开我们之外是否存在潜在的宜居世界。” “这部纪录片向使这一令人难以置信的使命成为可能的聪明才智、团队合作和奉献精神致敬。”

paras.en: “The Europa Concept” takes audiences through the highs and lows alongside the thousands more who made Europa Clipper’s journey to the launch pad a success — and who will, in the coming years, be there to share the mission’s findings about humanity’s place in the cosmos.
paras.zh: “欧罗巴概念”带领观众经历了高潮和低谷，与成千上万的人一起经历了欧罗巴快艇的发射台之旅取得了成功，并且在未来几年里，他们将在那里分享这次任务关于人类在宇宙中的地位的发现。

paras.en: Find “The Europa Concept” on NASA+ here:
paras.zh: 在 NASA+ 上找到“欧罗巴概念”：

paras.en: Managed by Caltech in Pasadena, California, JPL leads the development of the Europa Clipper mission in partnership with the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland, for NASA. The main spacecraft body was designed by APL in collaboration with JPL and NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, and NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia. The Planetary Missions Program Office at NASA Marshall executes program management of the Europa Clipper mission. NASA’s Launch Services Program, based at Kennedy, managed the launch service for the Europa Clipper spacecraft.
paras.zh: 喷气推进实验室由加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳市的加州理工学院管理，与美国宇航局位于马里兰州劳雷尔的约翰霍普金斯大学应用物理实验室 (APL) 合作，领导欧罗巴快船任务的开发。主航天器主体由 APL 与喷气推进实验室、美国宇航局位于马里兰州格林贝尔特的戈达德太空飞行中心、美国宇航局位于阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔的马歇尔太空飞行中心以及美国宇航局位于弗吉尼亚州汉普顿的兰利研究中心合作设计。美国宇航局马歇尔行星任务计划办公室负责执行欧罗巴快船任务的计划管理。美国宇航局的发射服务计划位于肯尼迪，负责管理欧罗巴快艇航天器的发射服务。
